texts.error.engine_did_not_open_its: The engine did not open its sound device.
texts.error.engine_did_not_start_legacy: The engine did not start: the data pack is not a Retro Engine v3 or v4 game's.
texts.error.game_s_data_file_missing: The game's data pack (%1) is not there.
texts.error.is_not_a_retro_engine_data: %1 is not a Retro Engine data file: it is %2 bytes long.
texts.error.is_not_a_retro_engine_pack: %1 is not a Retro Engine data pack: it does not start with RSDKv3, RSDKv4 or RSDKv5. This core plays only the packs of Sonic Origins. If it is a data pack of the 2011 release of Sonic CD, the rsdkv3 core plays it. A zip of the game's unpacked Data folder is taken too.
texts.error.is_too_large_bytes_for_the: %1 is too large (%2 bytes) for the core's memory.
texts.error.pack_is_from_2013_release: %1 is a data pack of the 2013 release of Sonic 1 or Sonic 2 (it starts with RSDKvB). This core plays only the packs of Sonic Origins. The rsdkv4 core plays this pack.
texts.error.pack_is_not_v3_or_v4: %1 is a Retro Engine v%2 data pack. This core plays the v3 and v4 games of Sonic Origins (Sonic 1, Sonic 2 and Sonic CD). A v5 game's logic is a program that this core does not have.
texts.error.save_data_could_not_be: The save data %1 could not be opened.
texts.error.save_data_has_more_than: The save data has more than %1 files.
texts.error.save_data_is_not_one_this: The save data %1 is not one this core takes: Settings.ini is the project's settings, and a name is at most %2 characters.
texts.error.setting_screenwidth_is_it: The setting screenWidth is %1. It goes from 320 to 424.
texts.error.zip_has_no_data_folder: %1 is a zip, but no Data folder is in it: it has no Game/GameConfig.bin. The zip must hold the game's Data folder as it was unpacked.
texts.error.zip_not_readable: %1 looks like a zip, but it could not be read as one.
texts.firmware.sonic1u_rsdk: Sonic 1 data pack from Sonic Origins (Sonic1u.rsdk)
texts.firmware.sonic1u_rsdk.about: The game's data pack as Sonic Origins installs it: everything the game is but the engine. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash. It can also be a zip of the game's Data folder as unpacked from the pack (RetroED unpacks it), with anything added to it, such as the Music and SoundFX folders of an older release.

texts.property.engine_version: The engine mode the game runs in: 4 for Sonic 1 and 2, 3 for Sonic CD
texts.property.scene_time_ms: The scene timer (minutes, seconds and hundredths), in milliseconds
texts.setting.devmenu.legacy_about: Turns on the engine's developer menu (devMenu in its settings file) and adds a Dev Menu control that opens it (Escape on a PC keyboard). From the menu a stage can be chosen directly. It changes what the game does, so it is part of the project.
texts.setting.game.about: Which of Sonic Origins' older games the project plays. The data pack of that game is the project's firmware.
texts.setting.language.about: The language of the game's texts (the engine's language setting): English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (simplified) or Chinese (traditional). The game reads it, so a movie records it.
texts.setting.plus.origins_about: Turns on the Sonic Origins Plus content in the data packs (Amy, and Knuckles in Sonic CD), as owning Origins Plus does. Off by default, as the decompilation's licence requires of a build given out. The packs must hold the Plus content. It changes the game, so a movie records it.
texts.setting.randomseed.about: The number the engine's random numbers start from. The engine takes it from the clock when it starts (time()); here it is this number, so a movie plays the same every time. The dates the game writes into its records are this number too. A movie records it.
texts.setting.screenwidth.about: How many pixels wide the screen is (the engine's pixWidth setting). 424 is upstream's default, a 16:9 screen; 320 a 4:3 one. The width changes how far ahead the player sees and which objects are awake, so it changes the game, and a movie records it.
texts.slot.savedata.legacy_help: The files the game wrote, as Export Save Data gave them, under their own names. They are put in place before the game starts, so the game finds them as its own.
